pr_title: arch: sw_isr: store device info in the table and add funtions to access
pr_body:
Change the internal function to `get_parent_entry`, which returns the entire entry of table.

Store the parent interrupt controller device in the `irq_parent_offset` table, and added 2 helper functions to:

1. determine the parent interrupt controller based on the IRQ
2. determine the IRQ of the parent interrupt controller

Declare the `struct _irq_parent_entry` in the header and added so that it can be used to test the functions in testsuites.

> [!NOTE]  
> This change will increase the LUT size for build with multi-level enabled by `CONFIG_NUM_x_LEVEL_AGGREGATORS * sizeof(struct device)`

___

> [!NOTE]  
> This PR is spined off from #62907, to hopefully make it easier to review, and is required to fix #63465

> [!IMPORTANT]
> Blocking #62907
pr_comments:
@cfriedt @galak the `has-multi-instance` prop was misleading, I was using it as a shortcut to get the controller that this implementation supports.

This implementation doesn't support `INTMUX`, i.e. [intc_rv32m1_intmux](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/interrupt_controller/intc_rv32m1_intmux.c), a single instance of it has multiple interrupts as child:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/b4da11f92967256e6a451f519c739ec95ea6175d/dts/riscv/openisa/rv32m1.dtsi#L88-L177

I've updated the filter to grab the interrupt controller that is the direct child of `/soc` instead, to just get the root interrupt controllers
(changing the assignees since this does not change any bindings anymore)
Rebased for the fix in #64630 to remove the workaround

> TBH... we should probably start looking into DAG or tree-like hierarchy for multi-level interrupts so we can avoid making this even complicated in the future.

Where can I read more about this? Any existing implementation?

Maybe the Linux kernel? The idea is (probably) simple, where each interrupt controller is a node in a tree. For multi-level interrupts, each node is a child of some other node (except the root node). So you can have arbitrary levels of interrupts, and each controller can trace back to the root controller. Though, this is an overhaul of interrupt handling and is going to be a huge project... for soul(s) brave enough to tackle it.

> Maybe the Linux kernel?

Yep. Linux would suffice. Of course, it's mostly about the model. The model will also drastically simplify shared interrupts with a marginal increase in complexity. It's also more stateful.

Zephyr's multi-level model (maybe surprisingly) started out simple too, of course 🤪

issue_context.title: arch: riscv: support for multi-instance multi-level interrupt
issue_context.body:
**Describe the bug**
Despite the multi-instance interrupt being supported by the Zephyr's multi-level interrupt encoding scheme, see [Multi-level Interrupt handling](https://docs.zephyrproject.org/latest/kernel/services/interrupts.html#id2), multiple instances of [`intc_plic`](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/drivers/interrupt_controller/intc_plic.c) is currently not possible due to the way that the `irq` number is passed into the `riscv_plic_*` APIs, see [1](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/common/soc_common_irq.c#L49), [2](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/common/soc_common_irq.c#L70), [3](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/common/soc_common_irq.c#L91), [4](https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/main/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/common/soc_common_irq.c#L107).

The multi-level encoded `irq` has its level 1 information stripped off before passed into an interrupt controller:

https://github.com/zephyrproject-rtos/zephyr/blob/e11bc94a44adabc6e29c74e2c903083e42bf0991/soc/riscv/riscv-privileged/common/soc_common_irq.c#L41-L53

This made it impossible for any driver, including out-of-tree ones, to differentiate an `irq` that is originated from one instance and another.

Please also mention any information which could help others to understand
the problem you're facing:
 - What target platform are you using?
    - Out-of-tree RISCV board
 - What have you tried to diagnose or workaround this issue?
    - There is no other way around modifying Zephyr source

**To Reproduce**
Steps to reproduce the behavior:
1. Build an out-of-tree RISCV board with interrupt controller driver that support multiple instances
2. Have some devices or software that depend on more than one interrupt controllers
3. Only one interrupt controller and its dependants work

**Expected behavior**
Both interrupt controllers and their dependants should work, since that is supported by Zephyr multi-level interrupt scheme.

**Impact**
Showstopper for applications that require multiple instances of interrupt controller on RISCV arch.

**Environment (please complete the following information):**
 - OS: MacOS
 - Toolchain: Zephyr SDK
 - Commit SHA e11bc94a44adabc6e29c74e2c903083e42bf0991

review_comments:
Does this need to be conditionally defined?

E.g. can we remove the ifdef above, use `if (IS_ENABLED())` elsewhere, and let the linker discard unused code and data?
yeah it fails to compile as the initialization used some undefined macros when 3rd level isn't enabled
I've moved the helper functions into an internal header, is this what you meant? @nashif

yeah, I may have overreacted to the sight of z_ APIs, it seems this header is full of them already. Need to spend some time on this and see what the status of the header and if it needs to be in the public domain in the first place. thanks.
